findings.title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). However, the only method with that name in the class hierarchy is the one added in UsernamePasswordForm: `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a UserModel argument. UsernameForm defines no no-arg overload itself, so this code fails to compile ('required: UserModel, found: no arguments'). Either the call should pass `context.getUser()` or a no-arg overload must be added; as written, the module does not build.

findings.title: user != null check removes conditional passkeys UI from the normal (first) login page
findings.body: The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, and it now gates `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137). During a regular first login the user is not yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`), so fillContextForm is never called, the ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute is never set, and the `webauth` form / passkeys autofill no longer renders on the initial login page — exactly the case the old code handled (fillContextForm was previously invoked in the user==null branch). The same regression hits the page re-rendered after a failed first-login password attempt, since the user is cleared there too. This also contradicts the PR's own tests, which assert the webauth form is present on the initial, not-yet-authenticated login page (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithExternalKey, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey line 194), so those tests would fail. The condition should only require passkeys to be enabled, not a pre-set user.
